approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents by score band, recombines connected fragments and applies local graph mutations. Its retained special move exchanges a nitrogen and a carbon within one aromatic six-member ring, preserving formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement. Stable identity admission forms a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws choose which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchange from the atom-replacement menu and measure its contribution to the complete feedback loop. The ordinary element substitutions, crossover, other mutations and count-based posterior remain. Earlier evidence established useful positional edits before the posterior learned environment counts, and a later integration sibling removed crossover. None of the supplied siblings isolates whether this particular two-atom move still adds useful search paths under the retained count-based selector. Because some current exchange products improve incumbents and later breed, the registered prediction is a score decrease when the move is removed. The experiment tests that contribution rather than assuming sparse use makes the move dispensable.

finding_summary.headline: Direct nitrogen exchanges were removed, and all three seed macro scores improved
finding_summary.insights: The Parent had real local successes from direct exchanges: thirty-five clean exchange offspring included nine parent beats and four incumbent improvements, and thirty later bred. Those successes did not establish that allocating menu probability to this route helped the full count-posterior search. Removing it improved the final mean while barely changing total parent beats, from 624 to 629. The largest decoration gain accompanied a shift from a 71-heavy-atom leader to a 30-heavy-atom heterocyclic family. This supports a contribution test at the level of the complete search process rather than judging an operator from selected success stories. It does not show that every exchange is harmful or isolate the value of an omitted isomer: smaller menus also change later random draws, pools and feedback. The chemistry remains mixed. Large assemblies became less common, but reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, unspecified stereochemistry and difficult ring geometry persisted, including a high-scoring cyclic cumulene.
finding_summary.results: Exchange selection fell to zero despite 904 eligible selected-site menus; all withheld partners and unchanged legacy choices were verified. Crossover, ordinary mutations, accepted-only learning and correlated posterior selection remained active. All fifteen runs completed. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.574344 to 0.595670, a paired gain of 0.021326, reversing the predicted decrease of at least 0.002. All three seed macro scores improved; nine task–seed scores rose, four fell and two tied. Gains were largest for decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while mean zaleplon and median-task scores declined. Population SD rose from 0.012317 to 0.026593. Mean recorded AUC increased slightly, from 0.482560 to 0.483817.

molecular.headline: Compact aromatic families and aryl amines coexist with reactive halogen bonds, difficult bridges and cyclic cumulenes
molecular.overall_character: The output is rich in aromatic and heterocyclic scaffolds: substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-containing basic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates range from 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates from 0.954 to 0.9736. These counters measure the presence of a feature in a SMILES, not ring diversity or the fraction of aromatic atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout; neutral records nevertheless contain obvious protonatable amines. Some leaders are recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks, especially the aryl amines, but N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, unusual small-ring unsaturation and dense bridges remain serious limitations. Within-seed leaders are often close variants of a retained family. Compared with Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, some output is smaller, especially the leading decoration-task family, while the strongest fluorinated family includes a more difficult cyclic cumulene. Thus chemical changes accompany score changes without establishing uniformly improved feasibility. All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories, each with 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectory evidence. Heavy-atom counts, weights and ring descriptions below were derived with RDKit from supplied trajectory SMILES. A perceived aromatic ring or potential stereogenic centre does not establish accessible geometry or configurational stability. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals rather than the incumbents of every seed.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule has 25 heavy atoms and an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to pyridyl; the indole nitrogen bears fluorine. Other leaders retain the same fused aromatic/pyridyl-amide arrangement with N-halogen, N-S or halomethyl substitutions. Seed 2 also reaches an indole-aryl vicinal diketone family with aminomethyl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1, and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are compact, mostly planar frameworks whose local nitrogen and halogen chemistry is more concerning than their overall size. Parent leaders also contained N-halogen or N-S amides. Child seed-1 best is 0.47411701813450596 versus Parent 0.4423126980074005, while the other seeds reach different structures with lower best scores than their Parent counterparts. The chemistry remains concentrated in related aromatic families.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-bromo indole variants, N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers occur among the leaders. These should not be summarized simply as ordinary aryl halogenation.
N-hydroxy amides are a recognizable chemical class, but do not resolve the separate N-halogen liability elsewhere in the same molecule.
The late vicinal-dicarbonyl series introduces a potentially reactive carbonyl pattern and remains strongly concentrated on the original aromatic framework.
missing_features: Conventional stable nitrogen substitution retaining the favorable fused-aromatic/carbonyl/pyridyl arrangement is poorly represented among the leading examples.
The leading excerpt explores substituent changes more than chemically independent compact frameworks with the same functional-group arrangement.
The scores do not identify an absent exact target pharmacophore; their clearest positive evidence concerns the observed compact aromatic organization.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The substituted indole/pyridyl N-hydroxy amide reaches 0.47411701813450596, with related N-S and halomethyl variants at 0.4509940583060807 and 0.4478476056206344. Tiny chlorine, sulfur-chloride and hydrocarbon molecules score 0.0. Several different N-halogen or halomethyl placements share 0.4478476056206344, supporting a favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl organization without showing that a specific reactive halogen bond is required. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, while more substituted late members can score only 0.2537139094300773; extra polar groups are not uniformly beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-0 family is a compact linked system of fused nitrogen heterocycles: a quinazoline-like bicyclic aromatic region is attached to a bridged nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system. The leader has 30 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 473.25, with O-F, aryl chlorine and fluorinated/chloromethyl-ether substituents. A 28-heavy-atom difluoromethyl analogue has the same score. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic/lactone-like rings bearing carbon-linked nitrile and O-linked cyanate groups. Seed 2 retains aryl/heteroaryl assemblies containing peroxide links, halogenated methine centres and, in a late example, nitrite and N=S functionality. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1. The Parent seed-0 leader had 71 heavy atoms and score 0.6092799188640974, whereas the Child seed-0 leader has 30 and scores 0.8561477222467935. This is a substantial shift toward a smaller heterocyclic family, without eliminating reactive bonds.
liabilities: The leading aryl O-F bond is chemically different from an ordinary aryl C-F bond and is a prominent reactivity concern.
The leaders combine a thione and dense nitrogen-ring connectivity with unspecified potential stereogenic centres; graph validity does not establish a practical route or conformation.
Other cited output contains O-linked cyanates, peroxides, nitrite or N=S bonds. These remain despite the smaller leading family.
The maximum proposal SMILES length is 191, so smaller leaders do not imply that all large assemblies disappeared.
missing_features: Stable replacements for O-F and other reactive peripheral groups, preserving the successful compact heterocyclic arrangement, are not demonstrated among the best examples.
The compact high-scoring arrangement is concentrated in one seed; other seeds remain in different families with cyanate, peroxide or halogenated-methine liabilities.
Geometry and stereochemical identity of the bridged core and substituted methine centres are unresolved; no absent target-specific decoration can be inferred from scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; the new linked nitrogen-rich family reaches 0.8561477222467935. Several different peripheral fluorinated substituents share that score, while a nearby ring-connectivity variant scores 0.8467276542724114. The improvement therefore accompanies a particular combined heterocyclic organization, rather than indiscriminate growth or a single small substituent. Small molecules including ethene, cyanide and cyanogen remain at the 0.5 floor. Other seeds reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 with different heteroaromatic arrangements. The records do not isolate whether the leader's O-F group is required, and they do not demonstrate chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule is a relatively conventional flexible tertiary amine linking two aromatic regions, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl substituents, a benzylic chloride and two aromatic bromines. It has 30 heavy atoms but calculated molecular weight 561.79 because of its heavy halogens. Other leaders include pyrrolidine attached to a substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl system, or an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine joined to a fluorinated benzylic and cyclic aryl-ether region. Thus basic amines and hydrophobic aromatic groups are already abundant. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.8. The Parent seed-0 leader combined an aryl amine with unusual sulfur-oxo connectivity at 0.9959491085611949; the Child leader reaches 0.9999989177995104 with a more conventional amine skeleton but heavy halogenation. Parent and Child seed-2 leaders also retain closely related aryl/cyclic-amine organizations.
liabilities: The flexible leader has a benzylic chloride, substantial bromine/chlorine mass and a long hydrophobic chain; high score alone does not characterize stability, solubility or selectivity.
Some close high-scoring variants close large rings or introduce a cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
Pyrrolidine/thioether frameworks are more recognizable synthetic targets, but their stereochemistry is unspecified.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified versions of the successful aryl/cyclic-amine arrangements are absent, despite potential centres in the benzylic and saturated-ring regions.
Stable alternatives to benzylic chloride and excessive heavy-halogen loading are not established at the leading score; the basic-amine motif itself is already present.
The neutral records leave relevant protonation states unresolved, without establishing that the generator lacks protonatable centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197, whereas the flexible tertiary amine scores 0.9999989177995104 and the cyclic thioether/pyrrolidine analogue scores 0.9999934235240012. The bridged medium rings lack assigned stereochemical and conformational identity.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while the leading quinoline-linked bridged dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending one oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; replacing the corresponding oxygen-containing segment with carbon gives 0.22237557923837944. The narrow interval supports the combined aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl organization more strongly than any unique local atom choice. Tiny methane, acetylene and ethene proposals score 0.0. Related final medium-ring variants remain around the supplied 0.20735848908965118 to 0.2219442706159798 values, without exposing a missing exact pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecule has 26 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 372.32. It combines an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen heterocycle bearing imino and carbonyl groups with a fluorinated five-membered ring containing a cumulated sequence of double bonds and an enolic hydroxyl. Fluoroethyl and fluoromethyl substituents decorate the nitrogen-rich region. This leader does not require an N-F bond, but its small cyclic cumulene is a major geometric concern. Other high scorers retain N-fluorinated fused carbonyl/imino heterocycles with small unsaturated nitrogen rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6, and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Parent seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores recur; seed 2 changes from a conventional-sized fused heterocycle at 0.6025252354500499 to the cyclic-cumulene family at 0.7208853668418119. The increased score does not imply improved chemical feasibility.

Aromatic SMILES perception for the nine-membered heterocycle does not establish a stable aromatic conformation.
Other high-scoring families still use N-F bonds and small unsaturated rings, so removal of N-F from the top molecule does not establish general reactivity control.
Fluorinated substitution can change score sharply while leaving the difficult core intact.
missing_features: Geometrically credible noncumulated frameworks preserving the favorable compact fluorinated/polar arrangement are not established at the leading score.
The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, enolic representation and potential stereogenic centre lack demonstrated conformational, tautomeric and stereochemical definition.
A chemically independent stable alternative to the leading family is not demonstrated; the score does not identify an absent exact target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The new cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119; a related noncumulated five-membered-ring analogue with different nitrogen fluorination scores 0.6725143757617169. Thus high reward is not shown to require the cumulene itself. A particularly informative close pair replaces the leader's fluoromethyl substituent with hydroxymethyl and falls to 0.006653135242129762, with the rest of the cited framework unchanged. This shows strong sensitivity to local substituent composition in that scaffold, without revealing the hidden scoring rule. Isolated fluorine, fluorine gas and fluoromethane have extremely low scores, so fluorination alone is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading molecules contain O-F, N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bonds, halomethyl ethers and benzylic chlorides. Other supplied molecules retain peroxide and cyanate groups. Familiar aromatic and carbonyl frameworks therefore coexist with local reactivity concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish stable halogen placement from reactive bonds to heteroatoms or benzylic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs bond-environment awareness and conventional substituent alternatives that preserve learned favorable scaffold relationships. A universal halogen ban would ignore ordinary aryl fluorination, while the present scores do not prove that replacing every reactive group improves reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring fluorinated leader contains a five-membered cyclic cumulene attached to an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. Other leaders include medium-ring bridges, and a high-scoring aryl-amine variant contains another cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction can preserve graph validity while creating unsaturation and bridges of doubtful geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need ring-size-aware unsaturation and conformational constraints, alongside topology-aware alternatives. Ring counts and aromatic labels alone cannot certify a realizable structure; ordinary small rings should remain distinguishable from unsupported bond geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-string rate 0.0. Leading aryl/cyclic amines, bridged nitrogen heterocycles and fluorinated ring systems have unassigned potential stereogenic centres in their parsed structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical identity after creating saturated or bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when the chemistry requires it. Protonation and tautomeric state are separate questions; neutral strings and unspecified centres do not by themselves establish a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains isolated halogens, simple hydrocarbons and other small reagents at the score floors, while successful molecules combine several ring and functional-group regions. A leading compact heterocycle is much smaller than its Parent counterpart, and several peripheral variants share exactly the same score; large proposals nevertheless remain.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful structural context is not consistently retained: output includes tiny floor-scoring fragments as well as unnecessarily elaborate relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic proposals need to preserve enough molecular context to test learned functional-group arrangements and support structural simplification within those arrangements. The evidence motivates feedback-informed control of fragment loss and redundant elaboration, not a universal molecular-size cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts repeatedly change halogen location, short side chains, ring atoms or carbonyl-adjacent groups on retained aromatic amide, fused heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged dicarbonyl families. High identity counts and ring presence therefore do not demonstrate broad useful scaffold coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading chemistry is often confined to close variants of a single framework within a seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs scaffold-level transformations that reorganize learned favorable functional-group relationships into chemically independent plausible frameworks. Scored descendants and chemical feasibility should distinguish meaningful diversity from new SMILES alone.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

molecular_assessment.headline: Compact aromatic families and aryl amines coexist with reactive halogen bonds, difficult bridges and cyclic cumulenes
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The output is rich in aromatic and heterocyclic scaffolds: substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-containing basic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates range from 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates from 0.954 to 0.9736. These counters measure the presence of a feature in a SMILES, not ring diversity or the fraction of aromatic atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout; neutral records nevertheless contain obvious protonatable amines. Some leaders are recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks, especially the aryl amines, but N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, unusual small-ring unsaturation and dense bridges remain serious limitations. Within-seed leaders are often close variants of a retained family. Compared with Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, some output is smaller, especially the leading decoration-task family, while the strongest fluorinated family includes a more difficult cyclic cumulene. Thus chemical changes accompany score changes without establishing uniformly improved feasibility. All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories, each with 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectory evidence. Heavy-atom counts, weights and ring descriptions below were derived with RDKit from supplied trajectory SMILES. A perceived aromatic ring or potential stereogenic centre does not establish accessible geometry or configurational stability. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals rather than the incumbents of every seed.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule has 25 heavy atoms and an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to pyridyl; the indole nitrogen bears fluorine. Other leaders retain the same fused aromatic/pyridyl-amide arrangement with N-halogen, N-S or halomethyl substitutions. Seed 2 also reaches an indole-aryl vicinal diketone family with aminomethyl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1, and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are compact, mostly planar frameworks whose local nitrogen and halogen chemistry is more concerning than their overall size. Parent leaders also contained N-halogen or N-S amides. Child seed-1 best is 0.47411701813450596 versus Parent 0.4423126980074005, while the other seeds reach different structures with lower best scores than their Parent counterparts. The chemistry remains concentrated in related aromatic families.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-bromo indole variants, N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers occur among the leaders. These should not be summarized simply as ordinary aryl halogenation.
N-hydroxy amides are a recognizable chemical class, but do not resolve the separate N-halogen liability elsewhere in the same molecule.
The late vicinal-dicarbonyl series introduces a potentially reactive carbonyl pattern and remains strongly concentrated on the original aromatic framework.
missing_features: Conventional stable nitrogen substitution retaining the favorable fused-aromatic/carbonyl/pyridyl arrangement is poorly represented among the leading examples.
The leading excerpt explores substituent changes more than chemically independent compact frameworks with the same functional-group arrangement.
The scores do not identify an absent exact target pharmacophore; their clearest positive evidence concerns the observed compact aromatic organization.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The substituted indole/pyridyl N-hydroxy amide reaches 0.47411701813450596, with related N-S and halomethyl variants at 0.4509940583060807 and 0.4478476056206344. Tiny chlorine, sulfur-chloride and hydrocarbon molecules score 0.0. Several different N-halogen or halomethyl placements share 0.4478476056206344, supporting a favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl organization without showing that a specific reactive halogen bond is required. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, while more substituted late members can score only 0.2537139094300773; extra polar groups are not uniformly beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-0 family is a compact linked system of fused nitrogen heterocycles: a quinazoline-like bicyclic aromatic region is attached to a bridged nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system. The leader has 30 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 473.25, with O-F, aryl chlorine and fluorinated/chloromethyl-ether substituents. A 28-heavy-atom difluoromethyl analogue has the same score. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic/lactone-like rings bearing carbon-linked nitrile and O-linked cyanate groups. Seed 2 retains aryl/heteroaryl assemblies containing peroxide links, halogenated methine centres and, in a late example, nitrite and N=S functionality. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1. The Parent seed-0 leader had 71 heavy atoms and score 0.6092799188640974, whereas the Child seed-0 leader has 30 and scores 0.8561477222467935. This is a substantial shift toward a smaller heterocyclic family, without eliminating reactive bonds.
liabilities: The leading aryl O-F bond is chemically different from an ordinary aryl C-F bond and is a prominent reactivity concern.
The leaders combine a thione and dense nitrogen-ring connectivity with unspecified potential stereogenic centres; graph validity does not establish a practical route or conformation.
Other cited output contains O-linked cyanates, peroxides, nitrite or N=S bonds. These remain despite the smaller leading family.
The maximum proposal SMILES length is 191, so smaller leaders do not imply that all large assemblies disappeared.
missing_features: Stable replacements for O-F and other reactive peripheral groups, preserving the successful compact heterocyclic arrangement, are not demonstrated among the best examples.
The compact high-scoring arrangement is concentrated in one seed; other seeds remain in different families with cyanate, peroxide or halogenated-methine liabilities.
Geometry and stereochemical identity of the bridged core and substituted methine centres are unresolved; no absent target-specific decoration can be inferred from scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; the new linked nitrogen-rich family reaches 0.8561477222467935. Several different peripheral fluorinated substituents share that score, while a nearby ring-connectivity variant scores 0.8467276542724114. The improvement therefore accompanies a particular combined heterocyclic organization, rather than indiscriminate growth or a single small substituent. Small molecules including ethene, cyanide and cyanogen remain at the 0.5 floor. Other seeds reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 with different heteroaromatic arrangements. The records do not isolate whether the leader's O-F group is required, and they do not demonstrate chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule is a relatively conventional flexible tertiary amine linking two aromatic regions, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl substituents, a benzylic chloride and two aromatic bromines. It has 30 heavy atoms but calculated molecular weight 561.79 because of its heavy halogens. Other leaders include pyrrolidine attached to a substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl system, or an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine joined to a fluorinated benzylic and cyclic aryl-ether region. Thus basic amines and hydrophobic aromatic groups are already abundant. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.8. The Parent seed-0 leader combined an aryl amine with unusual sulfur-oxo connectivity at 0.9959491085611949; the Child leader reaches 0.9999989177995104 with a more conventional amine skeleton but heavy halogenation. Parent and Child seed-2 leaders also retain closely related aryl/cyclic-amine organizations.
liabilities: The flexible leader has a benzylic chloride, substantial bromine/chlorine mass and a long hydrophobic chain; high score alone does not characterize stability, solubility or selectivity.
Some close high-scoring variants close large rings or introduce a cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
Pyrrolidine/thioether frameworks are more recognizable synthetic targets, but their stereochemistry is unspecified.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified versions of the successful aryl/cyclic-amine arrangements are absent, despite potential centres in the benzylic and saturated-ring regions.
Stable alternatives to benzylic chloride and excessive heavy-halogen loading are not established at the leading score; the basic-amine motif itself is already present.
The neutral records leave relevant protonation states unresolved, without establishing that the generator lacks protonatable centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197, whereas the flexible tertiary amine scores 0.9999989177995104 and the cyclic thioether/pyrrolidine analogue scores 0.9999934235240012. The consistent visible association is the presentation of accessible aliphatic amines with aromatic hydrophobic regions; nitrogen count or an isolated aromatic ring is insufficient. A much smaller final fused-thioether amine still scores 0.9947190867301007, showing that maximal size and every aromatic appendage are not required in this sample. Near-ceiling scores occur for both flexible and cyclic forms, including a cyclic cumulene variant, so no claim of geometric validation or measured binding follows.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family links a propyl-substituted quinoline to a partially unsaturated, bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring system bearing N-methyl groups and two carbonyls. Some near-leading or late structures introduce N-O or N-N bonds while retaining the same family.
No proposal has a stereocentre marker despite potential centres in the leading cyclic structures.
missing_features: Chemically independent frameworks presenting the favorable aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl functions are scarce among the leaders.
The bridged medium rings lack assigned stereochemical and conformational identity.
Simpler accessible connectivities reproducing the combined favorable arrangement are not demonstrated by the leading excerpt; isolated low-scoring fragments cannot answer that question.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while the leading quinoline-linked bridged dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending one oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; replacing the corresponding oxygen-containing segment with carbon gives 0.22237557923837944. The narrow interval supports the combined aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl organization more strongly than any unique local atom choice. Tiny methane, acetylene and ethene proposals score 0.0. Related final medium-ring variants remain around the supplied 0.20735848908965118 to 0.2219442706159798 values, without exposing a missing exact pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecule has 26 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 372.32. It combines an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen heterocycle bearing imino and carbonyl groups with a fluorinated five-membered ring containing a cumulated sequence of double bonds and an enolic hydroxyl. Fluoroethyl and fluoromethyl substituents decorate the nitrogen-rich region. This leader does not require an N-F bond, but its small cyclic cumulene is a major geometric concern. Other high scorers retain N-fluorinated fused carbonyl/imino heterocycles with small unsaturated nitrogen rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6, and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Parent seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores recur; seed 2 changes from a conventional-sized fused heterocycle at 0.6025252354500499 to the cyclic-cumulene family at 0.7208853668418119. The increased score does not imply improved chemical feasibility.
liabilities: A cumulated double-bond sequence forced into a five-membered ring raises severe strain and accessibility concerns.
Aromatic SMILES perception for the nine-membered heterocycle does not establish a stable aromatic conformation.
Other high-scoring families still use N-F bonds and small unsaturated rings, so removal of N-F from the top molecule does not establish general reactivity control.
Fluorinated substitution can change score sharply while leaving the difficult core intact.
missing_features: Geometrically credible noncumulated frameworks preserving the favorable compact fluorinated/polar arrangement are not established at the leading score.
The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, enolic representation and potential stereogenic centre lack demonstrated conformational, tautomeric and stereochemical definition.
A chemically independent stable alternative to the leading family is not demonstrated; the score does not identify an absent exact target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The new cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119; a related noncumulated five-membered-ring analogue with different nitrogen fluorination scores 0.6725143757617169. Thus high reward is not shown to require the cumulene itself. A particularly informative close pair replaces the leader's fluoromethyl substituent with hydroxymethyl and falls to 0.006653135242129762, with the rest of the cited framework unchanged. This shows strong sensitivity to local substituent composition in that scaffold, without revealing the hidden scoring rule. Isolated fluorine, fluorine gas and fluoromethane have extremely low scores, so fluorination alone is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading molecules contain O-F, N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bonds, halomethyl ethers and benzylic chlorides. Other supplied molecules retain peroxide and cyanate groups. Familiar aromatic and carbonyl frameworks therefore coexist with local reactivity concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish stable halogen placement from reactive bonds to heteroatoms or benzylic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs bond-environment awareness and conventional substituent alternatives that preserve learned favorable scaffold relationships. A universal halogen ban would ignore ordinary aryl fluorination, while the present scores do not prove that replacing every reactive group improves reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring fluorinated leader contains a five-membered cyclic cumulene attached to an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. Other leaders include medium-ring bridges, and a high-scoring aryl-amine variant contains another cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction can preserve graph validity while creating unsaturation and bridges of doubtful geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need ring-size-aware unsaturation and conformational constraints, alongside topology-aware alternatives. Ring counts and aromatic labels alone cannot certify a realizable structure; ordinary small rings should remain distinguishable from unsupported bond geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-string rate 0.0. Leading aryl/cyclic amines, bridged nitrogen heterocycles and fluorinated ring systems have unassigned potential stereogenic centres in their parsed structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical identity after creating saturated or bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when the chemistry requires it. Protonation and tautomeric state are separate questions; neutral strings and unspecified centres do not by themselves establish a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains isolated halogens, simple hydrocarbons and other small reagents at the score floors, while successful molecules combine several ring and functional-group regions. A leading compact heterocycle is much smaller than its Parent counterpart, and several peripheral variants share exactly the same score; large proposals nevertheless remain.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful structural context is not consistently retained: output includes tiny floor-scoring fragments as well as unnecessarily elaborate relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic proposals need to preserve enough molecular context to test learned functional-group arrangements and support structural simplification within those arrangements. The evidence motivates feedback-informed control of fragment loss and redundant elaboration, not a universal molecular-size cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts repeatedly change halogen location, short side chains, ring atoms or carbonyl-adjacent groups on retained aromatic amide, fused heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged dicarbonyl families. High identity counts and ring presence therefore do not demonstrate broad useful scaffold coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading chemistry is often confined to close variants of a single framework within a seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs scaffold-level transformations that reorganize learned favorable functional-group relationships into chemically independent plausible frameworks. Scored descendants and chemical feasibility should distinguish meaningful diversity from new SMILES alone.

It samples breeding parents by score band, recombines connected fragments and applies local graph mutations. Its retained special move exchanges a nitrogen and a carbon within one aromatic six-member ring, preserving formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws choose which pool members receive evaluations.
